rows.title: Commit this plan
rows.description: Landed the 33-epic execution plan itself, activating the standing autonomy grant that let the rest of the program run session after session without needing per-step approval.

rows.title: Review-Round Merge Gate
rows.description: Auto-merge now waits for a dedicated CI check confirming no unresolved change-request review remains on a pull request, closing the exact gap that had let a defective release ship before.

rows.title: Build-Output Pruning
rows.description: The release build now deletes files that were removed from source instead of letting them linger in the shipped package forever, and a related bug that could silently corrupt this repo's own build during testing was found and fixed alongside it.

rows.title: Content-Verified Branch Cleanup
rows.description: Established a safe standard procedure for deleting old branches — checking their actual content, not just merge history — and used it to clear three branches confirmed fully landed, flagging the rest for the operator to decide.

rows.title: Agent Roster Integrity
rows.description: Found and fixed an agent template that had been silently shipping broken placeholder text, and added an automated check plus a non-zero exit on sync failures so a corrupted roster file can never ship unnoticed again.

rows.title: Ledger & status reconciliation
rows.description: Reconciled stale status markers across TODO.md, feature PRDs, and intake records with verified PR references instead of guesses, and corrected a feature doc that still falsely claimed nothing had shipped despite real work landing.

rows.title: Doc-ID link integrity
rows.description: Extended the documentation-link checker to catch references that look like they stay within the project but actually point across repositories, and fixed four real instances it found — including two introduced earlier the same night.

rows.title: Fresh-session instruction probe
rows.description: Verified a brand-new session really does inherit this repo's working protocol automatically, confirmed the agent roster still doesn't exist, and fixed a stale line-number citation found live during the check.

rows.title: Friendlier Unknown-Command Message
rows.description: Typing an unrecognized CLI command now prints guidance and exits with an error instead of silently falling through to the welcome screen, with its command list generated live instead of a hardcoded, already-stale count.

rows.title: GitHub as a First-Class Tracker
rows.description: GitHub Issues is now a fully supported tracking provider alongside Azure DevOps and Jira, with real issue create/view/close support wired into five spells instead of being treated as an unsupported fallback.

sections.title: Wave 3 — ADR drafts (draft → PR → park acceptance → continue)

rows.title: Secret-Detection Design
rows.description: Drafted the design for catching leaked credentials and org names before they ship — a pre-commit scan plus a repository-wide CI backstop — correcting two inaccurate premises about what scanning already existed along the way.

rows.title: Vendor-Neutral Customization Design
rows.description: Drafted the design for letting a hand-edited governance file survive a future update instead of being silently overwritten, after a research spike found the file assumed to need vendor-neutral treatment was the wrong one.

rows.title: Spell-Compiler Design
rows.description: Drafted the design for generating each spell's Claude Code stub straight from its real source file instead of hand-maintaining both, deliberately scoped to build time only — and found the "66 hand-maintained files" premise was already stale by the time this ran.

rows.title: Decision Acceptance Brief
rows.description: Prepared a full accept/revise/reject brief for the long-pending ARC-029 decision, verifying the incident that motivated it directly against the original record rather than relaying a compressed summary, and flagged that accepting it won't by itself schedule its own follow-up work.

rows.title: Generated State Diagrams
rows.description: Spells that already compute their own state — version drift, branch/PR topology, review flow — now render it as a real generated diagram instead of prose, rolled out across the CLI and multiple spells over six sequential releases.

rows.title: Session-Handoff Durability
rows.description: Work named in a session handoff is now also registered somewhere durable, so a single overwrite can no longer lose it — and a real bug in the fresh-install scaffold that could falsely trigger the new detection was found and fixed along the way.

rows.title: Spell Routing Layer
rows.description: Every AI client now sees a routing table on load telling it which spell to invoke for common workflows, backed by proactive-trigger descriptions on every spell command and a new standing lifecycle rule — a fourth, hook-based enforcement layer was deliberately deferred.

rows.title: Doctor Platform-Policy Check
rows.description: `spell doctor` now checks a repo's live branch-protection rules against what governance says they should be, verified against this repo's own real GitHub Rulesets — the Azure DevOps path is implemented but not live-tested, since no ADO remote exists to check it against.

rows.title: New Spell: Sync Pull Request
rows.description: A new dedicated spell handles the recovery path when the mandatory pre-PR rebase hits a real conflict, covering clean syncs, conflicting rebases, stale-lease rejection, and ambiguous handoffs, with both `spell-create-pull-request` and `spell-ship` now routing conflicts to it.

rows.title: Delegation UX (solo-operator mode)
rows.description: Autonomous self-approval permissions are now recorded explicitly in a per-repo file, listable via `spell doctor` and revocable by editing it, replacing an implicit assumption — this program's own standing authority grant became the mechanism's first real record.

rows.title: Full-Cycle Coordination Fixes
rows.description: Closed real coordination gaps in the end-to-end feature spell — migration-number collisions, missing real-data migration guidance, and honest documentation that no actual agent roster ships despite the delegation language — after confirming one of the three planned fixes had already shipped separately and didn't need repeating.

rows.title: New Spells: Ward & Scry
rows.description: Two new spells shipped: `ward` scans a repo for leaked third-party names and trademarks, and `scry` clears a brand-new name for use — checking both the outside world and this repo's own history for collisions — before you commit to it.

rows.title: MCP resilience
rows.description: A new standing rule: one abnormal MCP tool failure now marks that server down for the rest of the session instead of retrying blindly, backed by an optional `.mcp.json` scaffold and a new `spell doctor` check for per-server timeouts.

rows.title: Registry-driven spell catalog
rows.description: The spell catalog the README lists is now generated directly from the source registry instead of hand-maintained, catching a real drift where the README undercounted the actual 38 shipped spells — with a new CI check guarding against it drifting again.

rows.title: Research-doc capability
rows.description: Research findings and technical spikes now have an official home and naming convention instead of being scattered ad hoc, reusing the existing `spell-document` spell rather than building a redundant dedicated one.

rows.title: New Spell: EAS Store Deploy
rows.description: A new dedicated spell ships an app to the App Store and Google Play via Expo Application Services, backed by a new store-specific standards doc covering the durable facts that had no existing home.

rows.title: Compliance standards + spell
rows.description: A new spell runs a read-only compliance self-assessment against GDPR, CCPA, SOC 2, and HIPAA — backed by a new standards doc that is explicit it's not legal advice — and stops at reporting findings rather than attempting to fix them automatically.

rows.title: Governance tail batch
rows.description: A batch of governance fixes: a new rule requiring a diff before deleting a "duplicate," broadened leak-scan guidance to cover personal identifiers, a new spell that captures verification claims and corrections as a structured record, and a commit-trailer model that now omits an agent's role rather than guessing it when the roster can't confirm it.

rows.title: Delivery-Channels Research
rows.description: A research spike ran two live smoke tests on this machine — confirming that npm's own `node_modules` traversal picks up prompt files, and that a symlink-like junction can be followed — after finding the epic's own starting description had actually mischaracterized what the idea was asking about.

sections.title: Wave 5 — Unparked implementations & the big backfill

rows.title: Enforcement-Mode Labeling
rows.description: Every one of the 25 governance docs now states plainly whether each of its rules is actually enforced by a check or just advisory prose, closing a gap where only one rule in the whole repo carried that label before — the pass also surfaced several pre-existing doc contradictions, like a rule requiring "3 issues minimum" that the actual review spell no longer requires.

rows.title: Secret detection implementation
rows.description: Built the secret-detection design for real: a pre-commit hook and a repository-wide CI backstop now both scan for leaked credentials and org names using one shared rule set, installed automatically by `spell init` — along the way, fixing a real latent crash where a malformed config file could take down the whole `spell doctor` run.

rows.title: Customization implementation
rows.description: `spell update` no longer blindly overwrites a governance file you've hand-edited — it now three-way-merges your changes with the new version and flags real conflicts — and the CI/CD standards doc split into a vendor-neutral core plus an Azure DevOps-specific profile so the same pattern can support other platforms later.

rows.title: Spell-compiler implementation
rows.description: Every Claude Code spell stub now generates directly from its real source file instead of being hand-maintained separately, catching and fixing two real title-drift bugs in the process, plus a starter shared-fragment mechanism for text repeated across a handful of spells.
